raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Part of #43875 (items 26-33). Split out of #43585 so it can be reviewed on its own. It does not depend on the other two PRs (#43585, #44887).

Item 25 (Plucker rays in float32 for LingBot-World) moved to its own PR, as asked in review, so it can get a GPU check without holding these up.

## Summary
Fixes in pipelines and the model helpers they use. Item numbers match #43875.

26. The blank default texture and the bake buffers used `(width, height)` where `(height, width)` is needed, which breaks non-square textures.
27. `ImageProcessorV2.load_image` raised `UnboundLocalError` for an ndarray or tensor. ndarrays are handled like PIL images and other types raise a `TypeError`.
28. `DiffusersPipeline` output layout: NumPy videos were permuted twice, a nested PIL list kept only the first video, and several images from an image pipeline were stacked as video frames. A nested list is now stacked to `(B, T, C, H, W)` for every video.
29. `DiffusersPipeline.add_stage` took its arguments in the reverse order of the base class. It now swaps the legacy order and delegates to `ComposedPipelineBase.add_stage`, so it also gets the disagg role filtering.
30. SANA-Video always encoded the negative prompt at 300 tokens. It uses `max_sequence_length` now.
31. ErnieImage treated a `[null, null]` `pe` entry as a real prompt-enhancement model. It is treated as absent.
32. HunyuanImage3 ignored `--revision` when downloading weights.
33. Hunyuan3D picked an arbitrary checkpoint when several matched the fallback glob. It picks the first by name now.

## Tests
- New `test_pipeline_regressions.py` (CPU): 12 cases. The layout test uses distinct values per sample, frame and channel, so swapped axes or a dropped video fail. The ndarray case compares against the same image given as PIL.
- With the source changes reverted, 10 fail. The 2 that still pass are guards: a real Ernie `pe` entry is still detected, and the legacy `add_stage` order still works.
- Unit tests that import the touched modules (25 files) on CPU, PR vs base: 590 passed vs 578 on base. The same 5 failures and 4 GPU-only collection errors occur on base too.
- No tests for 32 and 33 (a passed-through kwarg and a sort). No GPU run; these are API, shape and loading fixes.

nodes.body: Hi @mickqian @BBuf, please provide a review for this pr when you have time. Thank you!

Please keep the implementation changes minimal and simplify the regression tests as much as possible. Reuse existing preprocessing/stage-registration logic where practical and keep the camera precision changes separate, as discussed above.

For the tests, use small deterministic inputs and parameterize equivalent representations instead of duplicating setup. Strengthen the existing cases to check batch preservation and actual output values, so we get useful coverage with fewer tests and less code. Please avoid adding broad test scaffolding for these localized fixes.

I reviewed the output conversion, image preprocessing, stage registration, and camera-conditioning changes. The nested-list conversion still drops all video samples after the first; the remaining comments cover a clearer output-layout contract, reuse of base stage-registration logic, and targeted tests. Please split the LingBot camera-precision change into a focused PR so the independent utility fixes can proceed while model-level validation is arranged. CPU function checks only; no LingBot/GPU run.

[P2] While fixing this conversion, could we preserve the entire outer video batch? `data = first` discards every sample after index 0. With two five-frame PIL videos I get `(1, 3, 5, H, W)` after postprocessing, whereas equivalent NumPy input preserves batch size 2. Please stack each video's frames and then stack the videos, and extend the existing layout test with two differently colored videos so both batch size and sample contents are checked.

+"""Regression tests for pipeline and model-helper bugs (CPU only)."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+from PIL import Image
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.pipelines.diffusers_pipeline import (
+    DiffusersExecutionStage,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.pipelines.ernie_image import ErnieImagePipeline
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.pipelines.sana_video import (
+    SanaVideoTextEncodingStage,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.camera_geometry import get_plucker_embeddings
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.mesh3d_utils import (
+    ImageProcessorV2,
+    MeshRender,
+)
+
+
+def test_plucker_rays_for_bf16_poses_match_float32():
+    """bf16 cannot represent pixel coordinates above 256, so neighbouring pixels of
+    a wide frame collapsed onto the same ray when poses were bf16."""
+    n_frames, height, width = 1, 4, 640
+    c2ws = torch.eye(4)[None].repeat(n_frames, 1, 1)
+    # Values exactly representable in bf16, so only the pixel grid can differ.
+    Ks = torch.tensor([[512.0, 512.0, 320.0, 2.0]])
+
+    expected = get_plucker_embeddings(c2ws, Ks, height, width)
+    actual = get_plucker_embeddings(c2ws.bfloat16(), Ks.bfloat16(), height, width)
+
+    assert torch.equal(actual.float(), expected)
+
+
+def test_default_texture_follows_width_height_texture_size():
+    """texture_size is (width, height); the blank default texture was built as
+    (width, height, 3) instead of the (height, width, 3) of a loaded texture."""
+    render = MeshRender.__new__(MeshRender)
+    render.tex = None
+    render.texture_size = (64, 32)
+
+    assert render.get_texture().shape == (32, 64, 3)
+
+
+def test_image_processor_rejects_unsupported_input_type():
+    """An input that was neither a path nor a PIL image fell through to an
+    UnboundLocalError on `mask`."""
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="Unsupported image type"):
+        ImageProcessorV2(size=8).load_image(torch.zeros(3, 8, 8))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "data, expected_shape",
+    [
+        (np.random.rand(2, 5, 16, 16, 3).astype("float32"), (2, 3, 5, 16, 16)),
+        ([[Image.new("RGB", (16, 16)) for _ in range(5)]], (1, 3, 5, 16, 16)),
+        ([[Image.new("RGB", (16, 16)) for _ in range(3)]], (1, 3, 3, 16, 16)),
+        ([Image.new("RGB", (16, 16)) for _ in range(2)], (2, 3, 16, 16)),
+    ],
+    ids=["np-video", "pil-video", "pil-video-3-frames", "pil-image-batch"],
+)
+def test_diffusers_output_layout_is_channels_first(data, expected_shape):
+    """Video outputs were permuted twice (np) or misread as a batch (PIL lists), and
+    several PIL images from an image pipeline were stacked as video frames."""
+    stage = DiffusersExecutionStage.__new__(DiffusersExecutionStage)
+
+    output = stage._postprocess_output(stage._convert_to_tensor(data))
+
+    assert tuple(output.shape) == expected_shape

issue_comments.body: Hi @mickqian @BBuf, please provide a review for this pr when you have time. Thank you!

Please keep the implementation changes minimal and simplify the regression tests as much as possible. Reuse existing preprocessing/stage-registration logic where practical and keep the camera precision changes separate, as discussed above.

For the tests, use small deterministic inputs and parameterize equivalent representations instead of duplicating setup. Strengthen the existing cases to check batch preservation and actual output values, so we get useful coverage with fewer tests and less code. Please avoid adding broad test scaffolding for these localized fixes.

reviews.body: I reviewed the output conversion, image preprocessing, stage registration, and camera-conditioning changes. The nested-list conversion still drops all video samples after the first; the remaining comments cover a clearer output-layout contract, reuse of base stage-registration logic, and targeted tests. Please split the LingBot camera-precision change into a focused PR so the independent utility fixes can proceed while model-level validation is arranged. CPU function checks only; no LingBot/GPU run.
Thanks for simplifying the implementation and regression tests and keeping the camera changes separate. LGTM, pending CI.
